input.add_to_description: Day 10 ~7:30 AM: fight at the north door. The crate broke; three of the Grey Cloak's pikemen (Pikeman 1-3) came at Kit. Wren left the reliquary's foot seated in the lamp socket upstairs with Brann. Wren cast Faerie Fire from the stair; Pikemen 2 and 3 are outlined, Pikeman 1 resisted. Kit is hurt (13/20); Sparrow and the Grey Cloak stand back on the shingle.

entries.text: notebook: updated The Gullspit Light

You drop through the trapdoor and take the third step above the doorway just as the crate gives with a crack like a snapped oar. The fight starts in one breath.

Kit is first. Her sword comes round at the lead pikeman, and it's a miss: a 13 against his chain shirt and shield. She spends your Bardic Inspiration on the swing, a 2, for 15 in all. It's still short, and the die is gone. The pikeman's spear is quicker. It takes her under the shield-rim for 7, and she's at 13 of her 20 hit points. Behind him the other two jostle in the doorway, unable to reach past him.

Then it's your turn. You fling out your hand and cry the Lantern-Bearer's name, and blue-green light blooms over the doorway and the shingle beyond. Faerie Fire is one slot spent, so you have one left, and it needs your concentration. The two men behind the leader are caught: both are outlined in glowing light, and anything that can see them has advantage to hit. The one in the doorway has twisted clear of it. He's dark and sharp-edged, and Kit gets no advantage against him.

Beyond the glow, thirty feet off on the shingle, Sparrow and the grey-cloaked figure haven't moved. The cloaked man has his head cocked, watching the light with interest. Sparrow is smiling.

Kit grunts without turning. "Tell me when you can spare a word." She's at 13 hit points, with Second Wind and Action Surge still in hand.

Your action is spent on the spell, and Healing Word would be a second spell this turn, which the rules don't allow. You can still move. The round is turning, and the next turn is Kit's. What does Wren do with the rest of her turn?

sheet.name: Wren Ashgrove
sheet.opening: Wren Ashgrove, a half-elf bard of about nineteen with a quick grin and a sharper tongue, arrives at dusk in the river-market town of Marrowford, a few weeks after fleeing the caravan of her mentor Corvin Tallowmere. She was raised by him as a storyteller's apprentice, and she left in the night at a river crossing with his ledger of forged tales sold to nobles (its pages now hidden in the binding of her road-psalter), a few of his best forgeries, and a head start. She carries a brass lantern-shaped reliquary of the Lantern-Bearer, a gentle road-god of travelers and tale-tellers whom Corvin worshipped only as cover; it holds a curl of yellowed parchment in an unknown hand that may be a true blessing or another forgery. She does not know if Corvin has sent anyone after her. Her ideal: stories should be free, and truth is whatever people can be made to believe. Her bond: find the nobles Corvin cheated and decide whether to expose him or quietly fix what he did. Her flaw: she can't resist a secret, and she lies even when the truth would serve her better. She has 15 gp, a rapier, a dagger, leather armor, a lute, a diplomat's pack with blank paper and sealing wax, and was raised with no memory of her birth family. The hook: as she reaches the market square, she spots a caravan wagon with Corvin's painted shrine-lantern sigil parked at the edge of town, but no sign of Corvin. A frightened young page in a minor noble's livery is pressing a sealed letter into the hands of the wagon's driver, and the seal looks like one Wren has seen in the ledger. Something is happening that links her stolen ledger to a noble house, and it needs a quick-witted liar to either sort it out or be caught in it. Open on Wren in the square, with the choice of how to approach the wagon and the page, and a locked iron-bound strongbox on the wagon's tailboard that she itches to poke at.

A charming liar with a sharp tongue who will bluff through almost anything with a grin

Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

entries.text: time: 12 seconds later: Day 10, 7:28:54 AM

The crate gives with a crack, and you're on the third step above the doorway with Kit's back below you. You cast Faerie Fire through the splintered frame. Blue light blooms over the doorway and the shingle beyond. Your spell save DC is 13, and all three pikemen fail their Dexterity saves. Each is outlined in shivering blue and glows on the grey stones. I put the cube just past Kit, so she stays out of the light. One slot is left, and you're concentrating on the spell.

The first pikeman jabs through the gap, and his spear glances off Kit's shield. Kit answers at once. Her attack has advantage against the lit man, and her longsword opens his shoulder, so he's hurt and reeling. The second pikeman hurls a spare spear over his friend's shoulder, and it clangs off Kit's shield too. The third is jostling for the door. Outside, the smooth voice has gone quiet.

Round 2 has come round to you. Kit is holding the doorway, fresh and unhurt. Sparrow and the grey cloak are still out of sight on the shingle, and the three lit pikemen are crowding the only way in.

What does Wren do?

line:
"A word, Sparrow? Gladly." I keep Ember still and the staff upright, and call to the grey figure, clear enough to carry down the causeway and into the reeds. "Sir, your man says you'd like a word, so take off your hood, let's use your own name, and tell me what you want with a girl and her mother's lamp."

I let that sit a breath, then add, "Because I've been to Thornhallow's register, sir, and Aldous Verrel the younger was baptised a servant's child and buried at three, and his grave doesn't open for a man in a grey cloak." As I finish I swing the lamp-staff up and high, the signal, and cast Faerie Fire at the whole line of them on the road.

input.add_to_description: Day 15 ~2:06 PM: fight begins at the culvert. Wren named the register leaf and cast Faerie Fire (only Bandit 3 lit). Two crossbow pikemen shot Kit down to 0 HP (Bandit 2 crit). Grey Cloak backed behind his men, hood still up, calling for Wren alive. Guards await the staff signal, which Wren raised.

entries.text: notebook: updated Gannet Causeway

You keep Ember still and call it clear down the causeway: take off the hood, use your own name, tell a girl what he wants with her mother's lamp. Then the register, the baptism of a servant's child, the burial at three, and a grave that doesn't open for a man in a grey cloak. As the last words leave you, the lamp-staff goes up and high, and you speak the spell.

The tall man doesn't answer. His head turns a little, as if he were listening to something behind the words. Then he steps back behind his line and says one thing, quietly, in the gentle voice from the tower door: "Alive. Both the girl and the lamp."

Your Faerie Fire falls on the road, but the pikemen are quick. Only one, a lumpy man in the middle of the line, fails his save and stands outlined in violet light. The others and Sparrow shrug it off. In the reeds behind you, Pell's whistle sounds and the guards break cover, but they are a long run from the culvert.

The enemy shot first, though, and it went badly. Round 1 (Kit moved before you did): her crossbow missed with a natural 1, and so did the first pikeman's. The second pikeman's bolt hit her for 8. In round 2, Sparrow's shot at her missed, and Kit hit the lit pikeman for 10, leaving him at the edge. Then the second crossbow rolled a natural 20 on Kit, a critical hit for 16, and Kit went down at the wheel of the wagon. She is at 0 hit points and unconscious, and she'll roll death saves on her turns. The pikemen's blades didn't strike her because she was already down.

Now it's your turn in round 2. Faerie Fire is holding on your concentration, with about 55 seconds left. You're on Ember at the culvert with 17 of 17 hit points, two 1st-level slots, and three Bardic Inspirations. Corvin sits on the wagon bench beside a fallen Kit with his hands in his lap. The lit pikeman is nearly dead, three more are closing, and two crossbows are reloading. The tall man stands behind them with his ring catching the sun.

What does Wren do?

sheet.name: Wren Ashgrove
sheet.opening: Wren Ashgrove, a half-elf bard of about nineteen with a quick grin and a sharper tongue, arrives at dusk in the river-market town of Marrowford, a few weeks after fleeing the caravan of her mentor Corvin Tallowmere. She was raised by him as a storyteller's apprentice, and she left in the night at a river crossing with his ledger of forged tales sold to nobles (its pages now hidden in the binding of her road-psalter), a few of his best forgeries, and a head start. She carries a brass lantern-shaped reliquary of the Lantern-Bearer, a gentle road-god of travelers and tale-tellers whom Corvin worshipped only as cover; it holds a curl of yellowed parchment in an unknown hand that may be a true blessing or another forgery. She does not know if Corvin has sent anyone after her. Her ideal: stories should be free, and truth is whatever people can be made to believe. Her bond: find the nobles Corvin cheated and decide whether to expose him or quietly fix what he did. Her flaw: she can't resist a secret, and she lies even when the truth would serve her better. She has 15 gp, a rapier, a dagger, leather armor, a lute, a diplomat's pack with blank paper and sealing wax, and was raised with no memory of her birth family. The hook: as she reaches the market square, she spots a caravan wagon with Corvin's painted shrine-lantern sigil parked at the edge of town, but no sign of Corvin. A frightened young page in a minor noble's livery is pressing a sealed letter into the hands of the wagon's driver, and the seal looks like one Wren has seen in the ledger. Something is happening that links her stolen ledger to a noble house, and it needs a quick-witted liar to either sort it out or be caught in it. Open on Wren in the square, with the choice of how to approach the wagon and the page, and a locked iron-bound strongbox on the wagon's tailboard that she itches to poke at.

features: Darkvision: You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
Fey Ancestry: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep.
Skill Versatility: You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice.

Bardic Inspiration (d6): You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.  Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level. At level 2: Bardic Inspiration die d6.
Jack of All Trades: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

Song of Rest (d6): Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points.  The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level. At level 2: extra 1d6 hit points.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

line:
"A word, Sparrow? Gladly." I keep Ember still and the staff upright, and call to the grey figure, clear enough to carry down the causeway and into the reeds. "Sir, your man says you'd like a word, so take off your hood, let's use your own name, and tell me what you want with a girl and her mother's lamp."

I let that sit a breath, then add, "Because I've been to Thornhallow's register, sir, and Aldous Verrel the younger was baptised a servant's child and buried at three, and his grave doesn't open for a man in a grey cloak." As I finish I swing the lamp-staff up and high, the signal, and cast Faerie Fire at the whole line of them on the road.

input.add_to_description: Day 15 ~2:04 PM, Gannet Causeway culvert: the Grey Cloak stood unhooded-refusing at thirty-odd feet behind Sparrow and five pikemen, ring of leaf-green stone on his left hand. Wren named Aldous Verrel the younger's burial to his face and raised the lamp-staff as signal, casting Faerie Fire on the line: Sparrow (save 12) and pikemen 2 and 3 (5, 7) are outlined; pikeman 1 (19) is not. Fight about to begin.

entries.text: notebook: updated The Grey Cloak

You keep Ember still and call it down the causeway, clear enough to carry into the reeds: take off the hood, use your own name, and say what he wants with a girl and her mother's lamp. Then you give him the register: Aldous Verrel the younger, a servant's child, baptised and buried at three, and a grave that doesn't open for a man in a grey cloak.

The hooded head doesn't move, but Sparrow's smile does. It slips.

You swing the lamp-staff up and high, and cast Faerie Fire along the road. Violet light breaks over the line of men. Sparrow fails his save (a 12) and so do two of the pikemen (5 and 7), and all three are outlined, shadowless, and easy to hit. The third pikeman shakes it off with a 19, as does the figure in the grey cloak, who stands a few paces back from the light and is not touched by it. One spell slot is spent, so two remain, and you are concentrating.

In the reeds behind you, Pell's whistle goes up, and you hear the rustle of six guards rising to close both ends of the culvert. The gravel is narrow, the water hisses on both sides, and the wagon can't turn. Corvin sits very still on the bench with his hands in his lap. Kit has her shield up and her sword out.

Down the road the tall figure finally speaks, softly, so that only the first rank hears it, and the pikes come down level. Sparrow lifts his hand crossbow.

The fight is on, and the order of turns is yet to be set. You have two slots, three Bardic Inspirations, Kit at the wheel, and Faerie Fire burning on three of them. What does Wren do?
